x: We actually started two full teams and a depleted third and our "A" Team of James, Hall, Checkley and Newson were 3rd to Highgate with 38 points.

This race was the first of what is hoped will be a series of Inter-City Walks between the newly formed Union of London Walking Clubs and Continental Cities and following his fine walk in the Regents Park "15", Eric Hall was selected as one of the team.

Others showing sustained improvement are Eric Hall and Ted Smith and our team for the National 10 should be the best for a number of years. Congratulations to Eric Hall on once again winning the Civil Service 7 Miles Championship and George Checkley on his 2nd place in the Police 7 miles championship.

We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.

With two laps to go, Stan Vickers (50 secs.) who improves every time out, was in the lead hotly pursued by the scratch man E.Hall. They were well away from the field and Hall's superior speed took him first past the post with Vickers two seconds behind.
He was closely followed by Eric Hall and the constantly improving Stan Vickers who had changed from his usual claret and gold to those of the Stock Exchange for the afternoon.

Bangers, grilled to a turn, potatoes, bashed and pounded to insensibility by a team of master cooks, headed by such International figures as Messieurs Vickers, Hall and Goswell with a posse of Presidents to act as scullions.
Ash, Bare, Vickers and Hall please note !) (5) New records last year: 3 senior, 3 junior and 1 youth.

Our Stan Vickers, the Championship holder, started at a tremendous pace and at one mile had a lead of about thirty yards over a small group consisting of Eric Hall, Matthews (Sutton Coldfield) and Norman Read(Steyning), the Olympic 50 kms.

The Vickers Hall partnership receives such grand support these days that a successful future seems well assured. For if our younger walkers continue to improve at their present rate our club champions will be facing their toughest outings on home ground!

…Bhatia (9:9:0) 10th, and Mal Robinson (9:13:4) 13th being our scoring three. In the 5 miles Invitation walk Vickers and Hall were placed 2nd and 4th respectively behind a record-breaking Ken Matthews.…

Much of the interest in this event was lost owing to the absence of Vickers, Hall and Middleton. The most impressive of the Juniors was David Cocks who took the 440 (53.1) and 880 (2:02.2) in magnificently relaxed style.
There was a time when any talk of Belgrave walking centred upon Hall and Vickers. Then came Williams and Middleton to hog the limelight.

Hall, Bonser, Mathews, Baker, etc. - a band of stalwarts who with Lionel have travelled many expensive miles this season to take part in some gruelling events and have made sure that Belgrave has been represented far and near.

Winter or Summer whatever the distance Ray has held Belgrave together through many difficult moments and if the club is now enjoying its most successful period since the Vickers & Hall era of 1956-60 much of the credit for this must go to this cheerful colossus of the road.
Team:- Bicourt (6), O'Connor (20), Mann (41), Brien (51), Dear (59), Piotrowski (69) Others to finish:- Buxton (78), Rimmer (132), Hall (192)
Lawton, Hall, Picton and Dunsford filled 1st, 2nd, 5th and 7th places at Downley over 5Km., and Graham Seatter won the Luton 10Km. with Ray Middleton 12th.

George Williams, a wonderful stylist, former Belgrave walker and International was recently seen in Bournemouth and sent his regards to all his 60's compratriats; Messrs Middleton, Vickers, Hall, etc..,

Hall of Bedford eventually prevailed as Nick, in his own words, “hit a wall halfway round the second lap”, but he held on well to give the Bels an unexpectedly high placing after one stage – 3rd – ahead of a fast finishing Matt Shone (Woodford Green).
